declarations.name: registerDom
declarations.description:
Installs happy-dom's globals, once per process.

`bun test dom.spec` runs every DOM spec in one process, and
`GlobalRegistrator.register()` throws on the second call. Each spec still
asks for the DOM it needs rather than depending on a preload it cannot see,
and the flag makes the second ask a no-op.

declarations.name: withoutStyles
declarations.description:
The same markup with the inlined stylesheet removed.

Use this for every structural assertion. Declarative shadow DOM inlines the
component's CSS into the markup it is being asserted against, and that CSS
names every part, every host attribute, and every token the component uses.
So `toContain('part="media"')` passes on a selector, `toContain(
'data-scrolled')` passes on a `:host([data-scrolled])` rule, and both say
nothing whatever about what rendered.

This has produced a false pass twice. Strip the styles first and the
assertion can only see markup.

declarations.name: hostTag
declarations.description:
The host element's opening tag, for asserting on its attributes.

Reflected properties land here rather than in the shadow root, so a test
about what the host carries has to look at the host and not at the whole
document fragment.

declarations.name: hasPart
declarations.description:
Whether the shadow root contains an element rendered with the given part.

Matches the tag rather than the bare `part="…"` string, so a selector in the
stylesheet cannot satisfy it.

declarations.name: partTag
declarations.description:
The opening tag of the element carrying the given part.

Attribute bindings render across several lines, so this spans them rather
than assuming the tag is flat. Use it to assert on what a region actually
carries, as distinct from what the consumer wrote on the host.

Sticky and translucent, drawn on the material tokens so the page content
blurs behind it rather than being hidden by an opaque bar. The separating
rule and shadow appear only once the page has scrolled, which keeps the bar
flat against the hero and lifts it off the content afterwards.

declarations.description:
Regions are slots: `media`, `header`, the default slot for content, and
`footer`. An omitted region takes no space, so a card with only content needs
no wrapper markup at all.

`media` runs edge to edge and clips to the card's corners, so an image needs
no inset correction. Set `orientation="horizontal"` to move it alongside the
header, content, and footer stack rather than above it.

Regions are bare slots with no wrapper element, so an omitted one occupies no
space without the card having to detect that it is missing. Style slotted
content directly rather than reaching for a part: a header is whatever
element you slotted, not a wrapper we put around it.

members.name: internalOpen
members.description:
Uncontrolled state, `undefined` until the element is first toggled.

Deliberately not seeded from `defaultOpen` in `connectedCallback`: SSR
never calls that hook, so a `default-open` element would render closed on
the server and snap open at hydration. Falling back to `defaultOpen` in
the getter needs no lifecycle at all, so server and client agree.

members.description:
Requests an open-state change. In uncontrolled mode the element updates
itself; in controlled mode it only notifies and waits for the consumer.
